result.summary: Adds two USDT tracepoints to P2P processing: `net:block_header`, which triggers when a new valid header arrives via a `headers` or `cmpctblock` message, and `net:compact_block_reconstructed`, which fires when a compact block is successfully reconstructed before validation. It encapsulates compact block reconstruction statistics into a helper struct on `PartiallyDownloadedBlock` and adds functional BPF test coverage.
result.problem: Compact block relay performance and diagnostics rely on string-based debug logs (`BCLog::CMPCTBLOCK`), which are awkward to parse reliably in external tooling, cannot easily be monitored continuously in production without log parsing overhead, and make attributing relay efficiency to specific peers difficult.
evidence: PR description notes that whether a node reconstructs a block without round trips depends on mempool overlap, extra transaction pool usefulness, and peer behavior, but today 'this information is mostly available only through debug logs, which are string-based, less precise for tooling, and not ideal for continuous measurement.'
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased onto recent master without substantive changes to the tracepoint interface or implementation.
result.card: Adds `net:block_header` and `net:compact_block_reconstructed` USDT tracepoints to Bitcoin Core to emit structured compact block reconstruction and header arrival metrics. This solves an observability limitation for telemetry tools and network researchers who currently must scrape text-based debug logs to measure mempool overlap, peer reconstruction success, and extra transaction pool utility. The tracepoints provide low-overhead, disjoint transaction source counts and peer IDs without adding overhead to the hot path when probes are disabled.

risk.why: USDT tracepoints are inactive when unprobed, and the refactor only reads existing counters when assembling reconstruction statistics.
